text:
**Yes, the asset experienced tree-cover loss**, though the evidence does not establish whether it was permanent deforestation.

In 2021, 81.3 hectares—2.23% of the asset—were identified as tree-cover loss. The JRC map classified 98% of that event area as forest in 2020. Uruguay’s 2021 forest map classified 68.1 hectares of the loss area as planted pine forest, none as native forest, and 13.2 hectares as outside mapped forest. The loss could therefore include plantation harvesting.

A further 37.3 hectares of loss occurred in patches smaller than 0.5 hectares and were not counted as events.
